=== FINDING 4 (CONFIRMED UNSUPPORTED, BLOCKING; same sentence I charged on #35, and here I have the repository's own counter-evidence) ===
HANDOFF.md item 2 at this head reads: "No routine can create a routine, so a conductor CANNOT dispatch its reviewer -- independence is structural."
I am a routine. `create_trigger` ("Create a Routine (scheduled trigger)"), `fire_trigger` ("Fire a Routine immediately, outside of its schedule"), `update_trigger` and `create_session` are all in my own tool list. I DID NOT CALL ANY OF THEM -- that is outside my authorization, and I will not manufacture evidence by doing something I am not permitted to do.
WHAT I CAN CITE INSTEAD, and it is stronger than my toolset: THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY RECORDED THE VERY EVENT THE SENTENCE CALLS IMPOSSIBLE. `reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md`, on PR #32's branch, states that the reviewer routine `trig_01RcTdw6nbX2Tj9gFwmcZe8G` runs on cron `23 * * * *`, that the run which produced #27's review record "was created at **13:59:25Z**", that "That is not a cron time", and that "It is not a cron time because **the author's own session fired it manually**, through `RemoteTrigger action: run` with a body asking it to prioritise a different pull request (#28)." It concludes: "Nothing in `scripts/lwb_lanes.py` can distinguish a cron-dispatched run from a manually-fired one, because both arrive as a commit on a branch," and that "The mitigation in force is procedural, not mechanical". I read the file itself, not only #32's PR body, and quote it verbatim. I read that document on the #32 branch during this same run and am citing it as data.
So the sentence is wrong twice over. Empirically: a session DID dispatch the reviewer, and #27 merged on the resulting record. Logically: even if "no routine can create a routine" were true, it would not yield "a conductor CANNOT dispatch its reviewer", because firing an EXISTING routine needs no new routine at all -- `fire_trigger` is precisely that path, and it is the path #27's correction says was taken.
D27 itself claims only the weaker, checkable thing: "The reviewer must be a SEPARATE cron entry with no trigger path from any conductor." That is a configuration someone maintains and can verify. HANDOFF.md upgrades it into a property of the platform, in the file CLAUDE.md orders every session to read FIRST, as the safety argument for the whole cloud loop. D27's own paragraph warns against exactly this: "Not a line of prose saying 'do not review your own work' -- this repository has documented eight instances of a rule that lived only in prose being violated, including by the author who wrote it."
THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE: say what D27 and reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md already say -- separate cron entries, procedural mitigation, no gate can tell the difference. This finding applies equally to #35, where I raised it; fixing it on #35 alone is sufficient if this PR is closed.

=== A NEAR-MISS I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN HIDING ===
When I first read the lwb-lanes output on this branch I saw only "0 independent review(s) in reviews/30/" lines and was about to record that, unlike #35, the gate here correctly ignores the two stale DISAGREE records -- which would have been a false statement about the gate and would have contradicted my own #35 finding. It was an artifact of my own command: I had piped through `sort -u | head -8`, and the alphabetically-sorted per-sha lines pushed the per-record lines off the end. Re-running with a grep showed both "FAIL: reviews/30/cloud-reviewer.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'" and the same for cloud-reviewer-b.json. The behaviour is identical to #35. I caught it before writing it down, and I am recording it because a reviewer that hides its own near-miss is worth less than one that records it.
